title: Which customer support platforms support MCP? (2026)
summary: Compare customer support platforms with MCP servers and clients in 2026: Pylon, Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, Front, HubSpot, and Plain across Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT.
body_markdown:
Facts checked against each vendor's official docs and pricing pages on November 25, 2026.


Seven major customer support platforms document official Model Context Protocol (MCP) support in 2026: Pylon, Front, HubSpot, Plain, Intercom, and Freshdesk run generally available remote MCP servers, while Zendesk offers a generally available outbound MCP client and an Early Access Program (Zendesk Bridge) for its inbound MCP server. They differ in which AI clients work out of the box (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, and CLI coding tools), how they authenticate (per-user OAuth vs. API keys), and whether external AI tools can send customer-visible replies or only post internal notes. If you specifically want a ChatGPT-focused walkthrough, see[Customer support platforms that work with ChatGPT and MCP](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/mcp-ai-agents) .


Quick note on names: Intercom is the help desk, and Fin is the AI agent (the company formerly called Intercom renamed to Fin in May 2026, and Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin on September 10, 2026). We use Intercom for the help desk and Fin for the agent.


## What to check before connecting an AI client to your help desk


Most teams evaluate MCP for two different jobs. First, letting engineers, PMs, and support leads pull customer issues and account context into **Claude, Cursor, Claude Code, or ChatGPT** (an **inbound MCP server** ). Second, letting the help desk's own AI agents call external tools like Linear, Notion, Stripe, or internal APIs without building custom glue code (an **outbound MCP client** ).


Across the seven vendors below, four technical details decide whether MCP works safely in production:


- **Client compatibility:** Whether the vendor supports Streamable HTTP, official directories (Claude, OpenAI/ChatGPT), or Dynamic Client Registration (DCR), or requires a custom OAuth client or CLI config for tools like Cursor and Claude Code.
- **Auth and permission scoping:** Whether actions run under each signed-in teammate's role (per-user OAuth) or a shared API key.
- **Write boundaries:** Whether MCP tools can send customer-visible replies on the issue's native channel, update ticket fields, or only write internal notes and drafts.
- **Plan and action limits:** Whether MCP is included on every plan or gated by plan edition, annual action caps, or an Early Access Program.

## Platform-by-platform breakdown


### Pylon


Best for (editorial judgment): B2B support, success, and engineering teams that want both an inbound MCP server for Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT and outbound MCP Connectors for internal agents.


**MCP server and client posture:** Pylon documents both sides of MCP. The remote[Pylon MCP server](https://www.usepylon.com/integrations/mcp) runs at` https://mcp.usepylon.com` (US) and` https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com` (EU) over stateless Streamable HTTP, configured from **Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server** . In the other direction,[Connectors](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/agents/connectors) let Pylon's agents (Assist Agent, Slack Agent, and Automations) call external MCP servers or custom APIs with Personal, Shared, or Agent connections. Pylon also offers a direct[Cursor codebase integration](https://www.usepylon.com/integrations/cursor) where teammates mention` @Cursor` in the issue sidebar alongside connecting Cursor to Pylon's MCP server.


**AI clients, auth, and permissions:** Pylon's[MCP docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/pylon-mcp) and integration guides cover[Claude](https://www.usepylon.com/integrations/claude) ( **Settings > Connectors** , and Claude Code via` claude mcp add` ),[Cursor](https://www.usepylon.com/integrations/cursor) (` Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP` or` mcp.json` ), and[ChatGPT](https://www.usepylon.com/integrations/chatgpt) (native app in the **Apps** tab, plus custom MCP server setup). Auth is OAuth 2.0 or an API token (` Authorization: Bearer` ). Connecting requires the` MCP Access` permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Every call runs as the signed-in user or token identity and stays scoped to what that identity can view and edit in the Pylon UI.


**Read vs. write capabilities:** Connected AI tools can search and read issues, messages, and attachments (including images and UTF-8 text logs), create and update issues, update field values on issues and accounts, create or update custom fields and their select options, bulk-update up to 100 issues, snooze issues, post internal notes (` send_issue_note` ), and send customer replies (` send_issue_reply` , where tools are instructed to show the exact message and confirm before sending because replies go straight to the customer's channel). Teams can also manage accounts, contacts, knowledge base articles and collections, and read and manage macros, tags, and triggers. Tasks and projects, account notes, and call recordings require Account Intelligence; audit log search requires Admin (full history on Enterprise, 30 days otherwise).


**Pricing and plan availability:** The Pylon MCP server, MCP Connectors, Skills, and Custom API Actions are included on every plan on[Pylon pricing](https://www.usepylon.com/pricing) . Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month on annual contracts (monthly billing is available, with a minimum seat count for new customers). Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features (Assist Agent, Support Agent, Slack Agent, Automations, AI issue QA, and backtesting) require credits: commit to a yearly amount and spend it as your volume changes month to month, or buy credits as you go, and top up in Pylon anytime. Pylon is trusted by 1,800+ B2B customers globally.


### Zendesk


Best for (editorial judgment): existing Zendesk teams that want Zendesk Action Flows to call external MCP servers today, or are enrolled in the Zendesk Bridge Early Access Program.


**MCP server and client posture:** Zendesk splits inbound and outbound MCP. Its outbound **MCP client** reached general availability on August 10, 2026 on Suite Growth+ and Support Team+, allowing admins to connect external HTTP MCP servers (up to 250 tools discovered per server, 30-second tool call timeout) and run them in Action Flows, auto assist, and AI agents. Its inbound MCP server, **Zendesk Bridge** , launched in an open Early Access Program on November 10, 2026 at` https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com/mcp` alongside Agent2Agent (A2A) delegation to Zendesk's Monitoring agent. Zendesk also runs a separate ChatGPT support channel EAP (announced April 30, 2026) built on OpenAI's Apps SDK and MCP.


**AI clients, auth, and permissions:** The outbound MCP client supports OAuth 2.0 only (no stdio or unauthenticated servers). In Zendesk Bridge EAP, admins configure connections under **Admin Center > AI > External AI** using pre-built providers ( **ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Visual Studio Code, Notion, Slack, Antigravity, Lovable, and Pi** ) or a **Bring your own provider** custom OAuth client (which tools like Cursor can use). External agents authenticate with their own OAuth 2.1 identity plus user consent, and Zendesk checks both the agent's admin-assigned tool/group grants and the acting user's Zendesk permissions.


**Read vs. write capabilities:** Bridge's catalog covers more than 400 tools across tickets, messaging, users and organizations, knowledge, Admin Center, and Action Flows, with human confirmation required before mutations. However, during the EAP, pre-built providers are limited to 150 tools and one connection per provider, destructive skills, bulk exports, and third-party integrations are unavailable, and Admin Center tools are read-only.


**Pricing and plan availability:** Support Team starts at $19 per agent per month paid yearly, while Suite Team (which includes AI Agents and Action Builder) starts at $55 per agent per month paid yearly, with automated resolutions billed by usage and Copilot as an add-on or bundled in Suite Enterprise + Copilot. Zendesk Bridge and the ChatGPT support EAP are free during EAP, with GA plan packaging and pricing not yet finalized.


### Intercom (Fin's help desk)


Best for (editorial judgment): product-led teams on Intercom that want Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT to look up conversations, contacts, and help articles and leave internal notes.


**MCP server and client posture:** Intercom runs a hosted remote MCP server at` https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp` (US) and` https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp` (EU) over Streamable HTTP (legacy` /sse` is deprecated). AU-hosted workspaces are not yet supported.


**AI clients, auth, and permissions:** Intercom's developer guide lists setup steps for **Claude.ai** (connector directory for US, custom connector for EU), **Claude Desktop, Claude Code, OpenAI (ChatGPT), Cursor, Windsurf, and VS Code** , and supports Dynamic Client Registration with a redirect URI allowlist. Auth is OAuth (recommended) or a Bearer token (` Authorization: Bearer` ).


**Read vs. write capabilities:** The server exposes 16 core tools: universal` search` and` fetch` , conversation and contact search/get, company listing/get, Help Center article read/create/update, Fin audience listing, and` add_internal_note` . Intercom's documentation explicitly notes that` add_internal_note` cannot send customer-visible replies. Workspaces with **Fin Operator** also gain Fin Operator tools, but only when connecting via OAuth (they cannot be granted to Bearer tokens).


**Pricing and plan availability:** Intercom Essential starts at $29 per seat per month ($19 for new customers paying annually), with Fin AI Agent billed per outcome, Copilot as a per-seat add-on, and Operator inside the Pro add-on (credits). See[Pylon vs Fin](https://www.usepylon.com/competitors/fin) .


### Freshdesk


Best for (editorial judgment): Freshdesk teams on supported plans that want API-key MCP access from IDEs and desktop clients and can work within annual action quotas.


**MCP server and client posture:** Freshworks made its MCP server for Freshdesk generally available on September 10, 2026 (with standard limits effective October 5, 2026) at` https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp` . Custom domains are not supported.


**AI clients, auth, and permissions:** Freshdesk documents setup guides for **Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and Visual Studio Code** , and states it supports any MCP-compatible AI tool (ChatGPT is not in the named setup list). Authentication uses an **API key only** (` Authorization` header), rather than per-user OAuth.


**Read vs. write capabilities:** Freshdesk documents 38 MCP tools across tickets (` fetchTicket` ,` fetchTickets` ,` fetchSearchTickets` ,` createTicket` ,` updateTicket` ,` createTicketBulkUpdate` ), conversations (` fetchTicketConversations` ,` replyTicket` ,` createTicketNote` ,` updateConversation` ), contacts, agents, groups, companies, and Freshdesk knowledge base categories, folders, and articles. Because auth is API key based, teams should pay close attention to which agent's API key is used when enabling write tools like` replyTicket` .


**Pricing and plan availability:** MCP applies only to **Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (latest version)** and **Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026** . Growth starts at $19 per agent per month billed annually (25 actions/min, 1,200 included MCP actions/account/year), Pro is $55/agent/month annual (50 actions/min, 6,000 actions/year), and Enterprise is $89/agent/month annual (100 actions/min, 12,000 actions/year), with extra MCP actions sold in add-on packs. Freddy AI Agent includes 500 free sessions once per account before session packs; Freddy AI Copilot is a per-agent add-on on Pro and Enterprise.


### Front


Best for (editorial judgment): teams working out of a shared inbox that want directory installs in Claude and ChatGPT plus optional admin configuration via MCP.


**MCP server and client posture:** Front maintains two separate remote MCP endpoints over Streamable HTTP: the **Front MCP server** (` https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp` ) for conversation workflows and the **Admin MCP server** (` https://mcp.frontapp.com/admin-mcp` , open beta) for workspace configuration, alongside outbound MCP Connectors for Front's own AI.


**AI clients, auth, and permissions:** Front lists the conversation MCP server in the **Claude connector directory** and **OpenAI plugin directory (ChatGPT or Codex)** , and lists the Admin MCP server in the **Claude connector directory** . Custom connections for **Cursor, Claude Code** , or other clients require creating a Front developer app with a confidential OAuth client ID and secret because Front does not support Dynamic Client Registration. Auth is per-user **OAuth 2.1 + PKCE** , enforcing both app-level scopes (` read` ,` write` ,` send` ) and the teammate's inbox permissions.


**Read vs. write capabilities:** The conversation MCP server searches and reads conversations, manages drafts (` create_draft` ,` update_draft` ,` delete_draft` ), sends drafted replies (` send_message` , marked destructive), posts internal comments, assigns/moves conversations, tags, and updates contacts. The Admin MCP server lets company or workspace admins read and edit rules, inboxes, tags, templates, knowledge bases, and AI agent settings/simulations, with no delete tools.


**Pricing and plan availability:** Front Starter is $25 per seat per month billed annually ($35 monthly, limited to one channel type), Professional is $65, and Enterprise is $105. Conversation MCP rate limits are 100, 200, and 300 tool calls per minute on Starter, Professional, and Enterprise. Admin MCP is free on all plans during open beta (200 calls/min per company), though AI agent tools require the Autopilot add-on (billed per conversation). Copilot is a per-seat add-on on Starter and Professional and included in Enterprise.


### HubSpot (Service Hub)


Best for (editorial judgment): teams already running CRM and ticketing on HubSpot that want built-in AI connectors across CRM objects.


**MCP server and client posture:** HubSpot offers a remote MCP server at` https://mcp.hubspot.com` that powers its built-in AI connectors and is also open to custom MCP builders. (HubSpot's local Developer MCP server for building apps and CMS assets is a separate tool configured via` hs mcp setup` .)


**AI clients, auth, and permissions:** Built-in connectors cover **ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and Gemini** . Builders can connect any MCP client that supports **OAuth 2.1 + PKCE** (` client_id` +` client_secret` ) to` https://mcp.hubspot.com` , and **Cursor** is supported through the local Developer MCP server for HubSpot development. Actions respect the authorizing user's HubSpot permissions.


**Read vs. write capabilities:** The remote MCP server reads and writes CRM objects (contacts, companies, deals, **tickets** , leads, custom objects, and activities via` manage_crm_objects` , which requires explicit user confirmation before writes) and reads knowledge base articles and inbox conversations. One critical caveat in HubSpot's docs: if an account has **Sensitive Data** turned on, conversation data is blocked from the MCP server.


**Pricing and plan availability:** HubSpot Service Hub has a Free edition (up to 2 users), with Service Hub Starter starting at $7 per seat per month billed annually ($20 monthly). Professional and Enterprise add Breeze Customer Agent, help desk workspace, and SLAs alongside mandatory onboarding fees and **HubSpot Credits** for usage-based AI features.


### Plain


Best for (editorial judgment): technical B2B support teams that want OAuth-authenticated MCP access across threads, workflows, and interactive in-chat views.


**MCP server and client posture:** Plain hosts a remote MCP server at` https://mcp.plain.com/mcp` and also offers Connected Agents and Sidekick plugins for workflows inside Plain.


**AI clients, auth, and permissions:** Plain documents setup for **ChatGPT** (official plugin), **Cursor** (` ~/.cursor/mcp.json` ), **Claude.ai** (custom connector), **Claude Code** (using` mcp-remote` ), and **fx** , with unified Agents page setup guides for Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor. Auth is **OAuth only** (no API keys; requires` openid` and` offline_access` scopes), scoped to each user's Plain role.


**Read vs. write capabilities:** Plain documents nearly 400 tools covering threads,` Reply To Thread` (email, Slack, and forms), customers and accounts, labels, tasks, Help Center articles, workflows, broadcasts, SLAs, and Sidekick Agent discussions. Built on MCP Apps, Plain can also render interactive` showThread` ,` showWorkflow` , and` showLabels` views directly inside Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, and ChatGPT. Account administration (API keys, billing, roles, invites, webhooks, custom domains) stays in the Plain web app.


**Pricing and plan availability:** Plain Foundation is $45 per user per month billed annually (up to 5 member seats) and Horizon is $99 per user per month billed annually; Frontier is custom. AI agents (Customer Agent, Sidekick Agent, and Connected Agent) run on credits.


## How to choose the right MCP support setup


- **If engineering and support both work across AI clients:** Pick a platform that documents Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and ChatGPT with per-user OAuth and outbound MCP Connectors, such as **Pylon** .
- **If you want customer-visible replies blocked by design:** **Intercom** restricts its MCP server to` add_internal_note` and article edits, while **Pylon** and **Front** rely on approval prompts or draft-first flows (` send_issue_reply` /` create_draft` +` send_message` ).
- **If you need governance beyond shared API keys:** Prefer per-user OAuth ( **Pylon, Front, Plain, HubSpot, Intercom OAuth, Zendesk Bridge OAuth 2.1** ) over **Freshdesk's** API-key-only MCP auth.
- **If you are on Zendesk or Freshdesk:** Confirm plan and program gating early. Freshdesk restricts MCP to Standalone 2021 (latest) and Unified Omni 2026 with annual action caps, while Zendesk's inbound Bridge server is still in EAP.

## FAQ


### Which customer support platforms have an official MCP server in 2026?


Six major support platforms run generally available remote MCP servers as of November 25, 2026: Pylon, Front, HubSpot, Plain, Intercom, and Freshdesk. Zendesk offers a generally available outbound MCP client and an Early Access Program (Zendesk Bridge) for its inbound MCP server.


### Can Cursor and Claude Code connect to my customer support platform?


Yes, depending on the vendor's auth and client support. Pylon, Plain, Intercom, and Freshdesk document setup paths for both Cursor and Claude Code. Front supports Claude Code and Cursor through a custom confidential OAuth app (no Dynamic Client Registration). Zendesk Bridge EAP includes Claude Code as a pre-built provider and supports Cursor via Bring your own provider, while HubSpot connects Cursor through its separate local Developer MCP server.


### Which support platforms let AI tools send customer replies over MCP vs. internal notes only?


Pylon (send_issue_reply with approval guidance), Front (send_message on drafts), Plain (Reply To Thread on email, Slack, and forms), and Freshdesk (replyTicket) document customer reply tools over MCP. Intercom explicitly states that its add_internal_note tool cannot send customer-visible replies. HubSpot manages CRM ticket entries via manage_crm_objects with user confirmation, and Zendesk Bridge EAP requires human confirmation for ticket and comment updates while disabling destructive skills.


### How do support platforms handle authentication and permissions over MCP?


Most platforms use per-user OAuth so every MCP call stays scoped to what that teammate can see and edit in the help desk. Pylon supports OAuth 2.0 or an API token (requiring the MCP Access permission included in Member and Admin roles). Front and HubSpot require OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Plain requires OAuth with openid and offline_access scopes. Intercom supports OAuth (required for Fin Operator tools) or a Bearer token. Zendesk Bridge uses OAuth 2.1 agent identities with user consent, while Freshdesk uses API key authentication only.


### Does Pylon include MCP on every plan, and what does it cost?


Yes. Pylon's pricing table includes the Pylon MCP server and MCP Connectors on Professional ($89 per seat per month annual), Advanced ($139 per seat per month annual), and Enterprise (custom quote). Agentic features inside Pylon (Assist Agent, Support Agent, Slack Agent, and Automations) run on credits, which you can commit to yearly or buy as you go.
